description: Iterative deepening searches the root with alpha-beta, PVS or MTD(f) to depth 1, 2, 3 and so on, until a node or time budget runs out. It returns the deepest iteration that finished and discards one the budget stopped; the first iteration ignores the budget, so a move is always found. Each iteration tries the last principal variation first, and MTD(f) starts from the last score. Deepening stops early once an iteration is *proven*, because no line reached the depth limit. Use it whenever a move must be ready by a deadline.

papers.authors: David J. Slate, Lawrence R. Atkin
papers.title: CHESS 4.5—The Northwestern University chess program
papers.venue: Chess Skill in Man and Machine
